title: Comparison classifications are knowledge about differences
plainLanguage: When two examples do not line up, the important question is why: bad tracking, different view, a genuinely new pose, hidden anatomy, missing artwork, or a possible limitation in our schema.
purpose: Convert difficult comparisons into reusable knowledge instead of treating every mismatch as an error.

rules.statement: Use the existing comparison vocabulary and preserve uncertain decisions.
A comparison decision does not verify either source automatically.
Repeated “different view/foreshortening” decisions should motivate new perspective references; repeated “needs new artwork” decisions should motivate new part variants.
A possible schema limitation starts an investigation; it does not immediately change the universal skeleton.

implementation.futureWork: Aggregate repeated classifications into gap reports.
